Code map · PCB defect synthesis

CRG-DefectDiffuser Architecture

This repo generates PCB defect images. It takes a defect-free 256×256 board image and a list of class cx cy points, and paints one defect of the given class at each point while leaving the rest of the board unchanged. Two diffusion models work together during sampling: one knows what clean boards look like, the other knows what each defect looks like. The repo only covers generation; the training code exists but nothing calls it.

Repo: weihang-luo/CRG-DefectDiffuser Commit 724199e · 2026-06-14 31 Python files · ≈9,800 lines Paper: Luo et al., IEEE TCSVT 2026
Training data

The dataset: PKU-Market-PCB

693 photos of green PCBs. Each photo has 3–5 artificial defects of one type, and every defect is labelled with a box. The local copy is Graduate_Design/data/PKU-Market-PCB-corrected, a cleaned release with the same images as the original PKU-Market-PCB, which is the only dataset the paper uses.

The three annotation folders describe the same boxes in three formats. labels/ (YOLO) is the simplest, and it is the format the CRG repo reads.

Boards and images

File names follow board_class_number.jpg, so 01_short_17.jpg is board 01, short defect, photo 17. There are 10 boards, numbered 01 and 04–12 (02 and 03 do not exist). Every photo of a board is the same board with different defects added, about 99.99% identical. The defects were added by a program, not found on real faulty boards, and each photo contains only one defect type.

The three label formats

YOLO · labels/*.txt

One line per box: class centre_x centre_y width height, as fractions of the image size (0 to 1).

3 0.187376 0.588903 0.018787 0.040353
Pascal VOC · annotations/*.xml

Pixel corners of each box, plus the image size.

<size><width>3034</width><height>1586</height></size>
<object><name>missing_hole</name>
  <bndbox><xmin>2458</xmin><ymin>1273</ymin>
          <xmax>2530</xmax><ymax>1329</ymax></bndbox>
</object>
COCO · annotations_raw/*.json

One file for many images; bbox is [x, y, width, height] in pixels.

{"image_id": 653,

What's not included

  • The 693 rotated copies from the original release.
  • The original's PCB_USED/ folder of clean template boards. It isn't needed, because the areas between the boxes are defect-free.
  • A licence from the original authors, who never stated one. Academic use in a thesis is the normal case; cite Huang & Wei 2019 (arXiv:1901.08204).
Networks

The two models and their structure

Both models are the same class, UNetModel in guided_diffusion/unet.py, built with different settings from confs/pcb_gen.yml. Both use 1000 diffusion steps, a linear β schedule, and predict the noise ε plus a learned variance, which is why they output 6 channels. The sampler keeps only the first 3 (ε) in _get_et.

Contextual Synthesis ModelDefect Prior Model
Checkpointcheckpoint-256-defect-free.ptcheckpoint-64-defect.pt
File size · parameters606 MB · 151.6 M101 MB · 25.1 M
Input / output3×256×256 → 6×256×2563×64×64 → 6×64×64
Trained ondefect-free PCB cropsdefect patches, 6 classes
Conditiontimestep onlytimestep + defect class
Base channels · multipliers128 · 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 464 · 1, 2, 3, 4
Levels (resolutions)6 (256 → 8 px)4 (64 → 8 px)
ResBlocks per level2 down, 3 up2 down, 3 up
Self-attention at16 and 8 px, 32 ch per head16 and 8 px, 16 ch per head
Job in generationkeeps the whole board realisticdecides the defect inside the 64×64 window

256 × 256 defect-free model

64 × 64 class-conditional defect model

ResBlocks only ResBlocks + self-attention conditioning input
  • Read the diagrams top to bottom on the left, then bottom to top on the right. The encoder halves the image size at each level; the decoder doubles it back.
  • skip ×3: each encoder level saves its feature maps (after the input conv or the downsampling block and after each of its 2 ResBlocks). The 3 decoder ResBlocks at the same size each take one of them, concatenated with their input. This keeps fine detail such as trace edges.
  • ResBlock ↓ / ↑: with resblock_updown: true, resizing happens inside a ResBlock rather than through a plain strided convolution.
  • Attention only at 16 and 8 px: at those sizes every position can look at the whole patch, which helps with layout. At larger sizes attention would be too expensive.
  • Counts come from loading both checkpoints into the code with strict=True; every weight matched.
Reference result

What the authors' checkpoints show

The two checkpoints are the target for your own training: your models should eventually produce samples like these. Each model was sampled on its own from pure noise with 100 DDIM steps, without the CRG guidance.

  • Unknown: which boards the authors trained on. If boards 10–12 were included, testing their checkpoints on those boards is not a fair test. Your own models, trained only on train_board.txt, avoid this.
  • The scale (0.5×) is not stated in the README or the paper; it is confirmed by matching the authors' sample image to PKU board 01 (see "Data processing").
Phase 1

Data processing

The PKU photos are complete (every image has labels), but the repo ships no preprocessing and no training script, and the paper describes the data in three sentences: images "cropped to 256 × 256", "50 defect region samples (64 × 64) per category" for the defect model, and "approximately 3,000 defect-free background images (256 × 256)" for the background model. Everything else below is our implementation, in code/preprocess_walkthrough.ipynb (step 7, BUILD = True, about 2 minutes).

The steps and their settings

StepWhat happensSettingWhy
1 · SplitTrain on boards 01, 04–09 (541 photos); hold out boards 10–12 (152 photos)ImageSets/train_board.txtPhotos of one board are 99.99% identical, so a split by photo would leak the test boards into training
2 · ShrinkResize each whole photo, then work only on the shrunk image0.5×, bicubicMatches the authors' scale exactly (see below); 95% of defects then fit in the 64 px window, against 30% at 1×
3 · Defect patchesWindow centred on each box, moved by a random offset that keeps the whole box inside, clamped to the image64×64, offset ≤ 8 pxThe defect model's input size; the offset stops every defect sitting exactly in the centre
3b · Oversized boxesBoxes still longer than 64 px: enlarge the window so the box fills 75% of it, then resize to 64×64115 boxes (5.3%), effective scale 0.17–0.37×Keeps every defect instead of dropping the largest (mostly spurious copper); the scale of each patch is logged
3c · Paper subsetFixed random pick of 50 patches per classdefect_64_50pc/ · seed 0The paper's training size for the defect model
4 · Erase defectsPer-board median of all its photos (train and val) gives a defect-free template; pixels inside each box + 8 px are replaced by the templatetemplates/board_XX.pngPhotos of a board are aligned to ≤ 0.5 px and each defect appears in one photo only, so the median is clean; outside the boxes the photo keeps its own noise and texture
5 · Background cropsJittered grid over each cleaned photo: one crop per grid cell at a random point, cells shared out between the photos of that board, in proportion to its photo count256×256, ≥ 32 px from edge, 3,000 cropsEven coverage of the boards (spread 0.03 vs 0.10 when windows near defects are rejected instead); the 32 px margin skips the 0–27 px grey background around each board
5b · Verify and repairCompare every crop pixel by pixel with the template crop after the same JPEG compression; replace a failing crop with the same position from another aligned photo of the same boardany pixel > 10 fails, alignment < 0.5 pxErasing works by position: it fails on the 4 photos shifted 0.5–24 px against their board, and cannot remove defects missing from the labels, including thin unlabelled spurs. 38 crops replaced in two passes, none failed; 2,984 crops are now pixel-identical to the clean board and the other 16 differ by at most 10 grey levels
6 · Save8-bit RGB JPEG, quality 95, names <class>_NNNN.jpg and free_NNNNN.jpgdefect_manifest.csv, free_manifest.csvThe repo loader finds only *.jpg, reads the class from the text before the first _, and maps pixels to [−1, 1] itself

The scale is confirmed from the authors' own image

The repo's data/sample/sample.jpg is a crop of a PKU photo. Matching it against every board at scales 0.30–1.00 finds board 01 at exactly 0.50× (correlation 0.993; 0.58 and 0.61 at 0.48× and 0.52×), cropped at (176, 341). Our 0.5× crop at that position is the same image.

Held-out evaluation sets

Built on the fly in train_walkthrough.ipynb (Step 7) from boards 10–12 with the same scale, patch and rescaling rules. Background crops there are 8 random windows per photo that avoid every box (no template is needed for evaluation). The 152 photos are split by index into two halves:

HalfPhotosDefect patchesBackground cropsUsed for
selection76386608picking each run's best checkpoint
test76382 (60–66 per class)608every reported benchmark number

Checks

  • Loader: the repo's own load_data reads both folders and returns (B, 3, 64, 64) and (B, 3, 256, 256) tensors in [−1, 1], with class labels matching the file names.
  • Image statistics: our cleaned background crops match raw crops of the same boards and of the held-out boards in mean colour and contrast; edge strength is about 3% lower because erased areas are slightly smoother.
  • Erasing: 988 of the 3,000 crops contain an erased defect. On aligned photos no seams are visible (a missing hole becomes an intact pad). The template check (step 5b) found 21 crops with seams from misaligned photos and 17 with unlabelled defects; all 38 were replaced. Outside the defects, all photos of a board are pixel-identical, so the 256 set covers 7 board layouts at different positions rather than 3,000 independent images.
  • Authors' model on our data: its noise-prediction error on our crops (0.171 at t = 10) is no higher than on raw PKU crops (0.207 on the same boards, 0.161 on boards 10–12), so our crops are normal PCB images to it.

Where we differ from the authors, or cannot tell

  • Background crops: the repo's RandomCroppedImageDataset cuts a new random crop from whole images every time one is loaded, keeping a margin from the edges (crop_margins). The authors probably trained the 256 model that way, which gives far more crop positions than our 3,000 fixed crops. This may explain part of the overfitting we measured on boards 10–12.
  • Boards: which boards the authors trained on is unknown. Their 256 samples show silkscreen from board 08 and their sample image is board 01, both training boards for us; boards 10–12 cannot be ruled out.
  • Not stated in the paper: crop positions, the window offset, how oversized defects are handled, how defects are kept out of the background set, and any augmentation. Our choices for these are the settings in the table above, and should be reported as such.
Phase 3 · running

Reproduction experiments with the authors' checkpoints

Goal: reproduce the downstream experiments of the CRG paper (TCSVT 2026) with the authors' two released checkpoints: comparison with baseline generators, augmentation at 1×/2×/3×, an ablation of the guidance components, quality metrics, and tuning of the generation. The plan is in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-16-crg-reproduction-experiments.md; the code is in code/experiments/. Status on Mon 16 Nov, 16:17: generation and detector training are running in the background. Later results and changes are in the dated experiment log below.

The idea: synthetic images are judged by a detector

A generated image is only useful if it helps a defect detector. Every generation method is therefore evaluated the same way: its synthetic images are added to the real training images, a YOLOv11n object detector (box + class, supervised) is trained on the mix, and its mAP and recall are measured on real images from boards no generator or detector has seen.

real train crops (300 defect + 50 defect-free) ─┐
                                                ├─► YOLOv11n ─► real test crops (boards 10–12) ─► mAP@50–95, Recall
synthetic defect crops (0 / 300 / 600 / 900)  ─┘

Protocol: paper vs ours

CRG paper (Sec. IV)Ours
Real training set300 defect images + 50 defect-free, 256×256same counts, 0.5× crops from boards 01, 04–09 (50 per class)
Test set300 images, 50 per class, "distinct images"300 crops, 50 per class, from the test half of boards 10–12
Splitnot stated (probably by image)by board (decision D2): stricter, so lower absolute mAP is expected
DetectorYOLOv11n, 200 epochs, batch 32same; image size 256; best epoch chosen on the selection half; 3 seeds per configuration
MetricsRecall, mAP@50–95, per classsame, plus mAP@50 and precision; KID, LPIPS, copy check and time per image
Augmentation scales1×, 2×, 3× synthetic, class-balanced300 / 600 / 900 synthetic images, nested subsets, 50 / 100 / 150 per class
Generation settingsDDIM 250 steps, Tstart = 30, Nopt = 2the repo's pcb_gen.yml unchanged (same values)
Ablationcumulative CGM components; detector trained on 1,800 synthetic images onlysame steps; 300 synthetic images per configuration (budget)

Step 1 · Real detection data (build_detection_data.py)

Every crop is 256×256 on the 0.5× photo, chosen so that one labelled defect lies at least 8 px inside it; all other boxes in the window are labelled as well (boxes cut by the border are kept if at least half is visible).

SplitImagesBoxesSource photosUsed for
train350 (300 defect + 50 defect-free)380262 · boards 01, 04–09detector training (with synthetic data added)
select30036076 · boards 10–12best epoch of each detector; tuning in P7
test30037376 · boards 10–12every reported number

Step 2 · Generation jobs (make_jobs.py)

900 jobs, shared by every method, so all methods see the same background, class and position and differ only in the generated content.

  • Background: a verified defect-free crop from free_256/.
  • Position: the position of a real defect of the same class on the same board, taken from another training photo. Photos of a board are aligned copies, so the defect lands where that defect type really occurs (a short between real traces, a missing hole on a real pad). Defects longer than 56 px are not used, so every defect fits the 64×64 window. 751 distinct positions on all 7 training boards.
  • Class balance: class = job index mod 6, so jobs 0–299 / 0–599 / 0–899 are the 1× / 2× / 3× sets with 50 / 100 / 150 per class.
  • Label box: the size of the real defect at that position, centred in the 64×64 window. The papers do not say how synthetic images get boxes; this is our choice and is the same for every method.

Step 3 · Methods (generate.py)

Every diffusion method starts from the same point: the image noised to step 30 of 250 (Tstart = 30), as in the paper.

MethodWhat it doesRelation to the papersTime / image*
originalno synthetic data"Original (No Aug.)"—
copypastea real defect of the same class and board (+4 px border) pasted at the positionour reference; not in the papers0.1 s
dpmpastea 64-model sample (50-step DDIM) pasted into the window, no blendingour ablation of the dual-model idea0.4 s
repaintthe pasted image, noised to Tstart; the 256 model re-denoises the window while the outside is replaced by the noised background each step; 2 resampling steps"RePaint" with the CSM as backbone and 2 resampling steps, as in the paper; our DDIM implementation1.9 s
copaintthe repo's latent optimisation from the pasted image with only the background term (no defect-model guidance)"CoPaint"-style; approximation, not the official CoPaint code (paper: ~142 s/image)21 s
ecicsthe repo sampler with the attention mask off: loss 10·defect + 0.06·backgroundDEFectDiffuser (ECICS) Eq. 4; also the ablation base25 s
crgpcb_gen.yml unchangedthe full CRG-DefectDiffuser23 s
ControlNet, AnomalyDiffusion, DefFillerneed separate repositories and their own training: not reproduced; the paper's numbers are cited instead—

*Measured in the pilot on the RTX 4090 while our own diffusion training was running.

Step 4 · Ablation (CRG Table III)

The guidance-map components are switched on one at a time through pcb_gen.yml settings; each configuration generates jobs 0–299 and a detector is trained on those 300 synthetic images only.

ConfigurationSetting
ecics (base)attention mask off
abl_sig+ sigmoid activation (no blur, no connected components, no EMA)
abl_gs+ Gaussian smoothing
abl_ccf+ connected-component filtering
crg (full)+ EMA temporal stabilisation

Pilot: 12 jobs per method

  • CRG and ECICS draw a visible defect of the right type in the box (a hole in the pad, a bite, a broken trace, a bridge, a spur, a copper sliver) and leave the board around it unchanged.
  • Copy-paste gives real defects but with visible paste edges and sometimes a mismatched pad size.
  • DPM-paste shows that the 64 model alone does not fit the board: its patch has its own traces and pads, with hard edges.
  • RePaint and the CoPaint approximation mostly remove the pasted defect: guided only by the background, the 256 model (trained on defect-free boards) restores a clean board. Their label boxes then mark defects that are not there, which should lower the detector's precision. The CRG paper reports the same tendency (both lowered mAP slightly).

Step 5 · Detector runs (detect.py, run_pipeline.py)

24 configurations × 3 seeds = 72 detector runs: original; six methods at 1×, 2× and 3×; five ablation configurations (synthetic only). A configuration starts as soon as its synthetic images exist. Model weights are deleted after testing; only metrics.json is kept per run.

First resultmAP@50–95mAP@50PrecisionRecall

Our baseline is lower than the paper's, as expected with unseen test boards; comparisons are made on the gain each method gives over our own baseline.

Schedule and how to follow it

WorkSizeEstimateStatus (16:17)
copypaste, dpmpaste, repaint900 eachminutes1× done (300 each)
crg, ecics, copaint900 each~6 h eachcrg running
abl_sig, abl_gs, abl_ccf300 each~2 h eachqueued
detector runs72~18 min each1 done, 1 running
our 64 model (50/class) → 200kstep 101,500
our 256 model → 500k~27 h after the 64 runqueued
  • Everything shares one GPU, so all jobs run slower than alone; the full set is expected to take about 1.5 days.
  • The pipeline waits for free GPU memory before each job and pauses while our 256 training starts, so it cannot crash that run.
  • Progress: results/experiments/pipeline.log (one line per job). Results: results/experiments/detection/<config>/seed<k>/metrics.json. Rerunning run_pipeline.py resumes and skips finished work.

Still to do after the runs

  • P6 quality: KID and LPIPS of each method against real test crops, copy check, time per image.
  • P7 optimisation on the selection half only: Tstart 20/30/50; loss weights (the code uses 10⁵/10⁴/5·10⁴, the paper states 1/0.1/0.01); mask temperature; the likely bug t[0] / 10 == 0 (probably meant % 10); the scale of large spurious-copper defects.
  • P8: tables and figures in this report. P9: repeat with our own checkpoints once training ends.

Caveats

  • The authors' checkpoints were trained on unknown boards, possibly including 10–12. Synthetic data from them could carry test-board appearance; copy-paste and our own checkpoints (P9) do not.
  • Synthetic label boxes, RePaint and the CoPaint approximation are our implementations; the papers do not specify them.
  • With 300 test images, single-run mAP is noisy; differences are judged by the mean and spread over 3 seeds.

  • Reproduced: the no-augmentation baseline (0.497 vs 0.496), DDIM (0.495 vs 0.495) and CoPaint (0.487 vs 0.488) overall; RePaint and CoPaint lowering the score.
  • Not reproduced: the gains of CRG (paper +12.3 %, ours −0.5 %), DefFiller (+7.3 % vs −2.2 %) and ControlNet (+6.0 % vs −3.0 %). In our runs no method beats the baseline by more than the noise (about ±0.012 from the choice of 300 test images, ±0.005 between seeds).
  • Per class: our baseline is lower on missing hole (0.551 vs 0.616) and higher on short, spur and spurious copper; our baseline recall (0.936) is much higher than the paper's (0.869), so the paper's test set is probably harder. CRG's largest gains in the paper (short +19 %, spurious copper +21 %, spur +14 %) do not appear here.
  • With 10 real crops per class CRG gains +15 % and is the best method, ahead of DDIM (+8 %); RePaint, CoPaint, ControlNet and DefFiller lower the score. This ordering matches the paper; the gain appears only when real data is scarce.
  • Differences from the paper: AnomalyDiffusion not run; ControlNet is our fine-tune of SD 1.5 + ControlNet with a Canny edge map (box area blanked) and a text prompt; DefFiller uses full GLIGEN guidance for all steps (the official schedule produced non-PCB images at 256 × 256); synthetic box labels are the size of a real defect at the placement (the paper does not say how it labelled synthetic images).

2026-11-20 (Fri) · clues about how the authors prepared their data

Context. Since 18 Nov the main comparison uses split A (photos split at random, all 10 boards seen in training, as in the paper) with the detector at input 640. There the no-augmentation baseline reproduces the paper (mAP@50–95 0.497 vs 0.496), but the authors' CRG gives no gain (0.494 vs the paper's 0.557). The paper leaves most of the data preparation unstated, so the code, the figures and the authors' checkpoint were searched for clues. Full evidence: results/experiments/paper_figs/clues.md; scripts code/experiments/paper_figures.py and check_csm_boards.py.

What the papers state. CRG: "patches were cropped from the original images to a standard resolution of 256 × 256 pixels"; 300 training and 300 test images (50 per class); 1,800 defect-free images "cropped from the normal regions of the dataset"; 64 × 64 patches "cropped from the annotated defect regions". ECICS adds about 3,000 defect-free images. Nothing on scale, crop placement, cut defects, split level, synthetic labels or detector input size.

The same group's sibling method (DMGR) places the 64 window at random, at least 20 px from the crop edge, one defect per imageGen.py in github.com/weihang-luo/DMGR, lines 240–241 (verified)fact for DMGR

The sibling paper DMGR (IEEE Access 2026, DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2026.3661342), from the same group with the same data protocol, adds:

  • Detector settings: YOLOv11n, 200 epochs, AdamW, initial learning rate 0.01, cosine decay, one fixed seed. Our runs use the Ultralytics default, which picks AdamW at 0.001 with linear decay. Queued as a check (Original, CRG, DDIM × 3 seeds, split A, input 640).
  • Shared experiments: the baseline rows (Original, DDIM, RePaint, CoPaint, AnomalyDiffusion) have identical per-class numbers in both papers, and the 29 baseline images in DMGR's comparison figure are pixel-identical to those in CRG's.
  • Inconsistencies: ControlNet shows the same images with different numbers (CRG mAP 0.526, DMGR 0.492); DMGR's overall column does not match its own per-class values (Original 0.494 / 0.897 vs per-class means 0.496 / 0.869); the background model is trained 200k iterations in DMGR vs 500k in CRG.
  • In both papers a detector trained only on synthetic images beats the one trained on 300 real images (CRG 0.527–0.549, DMGR 0.521–0.535, real 0.496). In our board-split runs at input 256 synthetic-only was far below real; queued on split A at input 640 (300 CRG images, 3 seeds).
  • Same as ours: 0.5× scale, all boards in every set (split A), one defect per synthetic image, labels about the size of a real defect.
  • Likely different: how real test crops are cut. Ours always contain the whole defect, at least 8 px from the edge; theirs seem cut on a grid, so some defects would be cut by the crop edge, a harder test with lower recall. That fits the paper's lower baseline recall (0.869 vs our 0.936).
  • Minor differences: hand-picked defect positions (ours: real defect positions on the same board), and backgrounds reused across classes (ours: 300 different backgrounds).
  • Queued checks (split A, input 640, 3 seeds): B, test crops with defects that may be cut by the edge (26 % of main defects cut); B2, test crops cut on the 256 grid; A, best epoch chosen on the test set; C1, synthetic boxes as the whole 64 window or the changed area; C2, more defects per synthetic image. C2 is probably not the paper's setup, given the one-defect-per-image finding.

2026-11-17 (Tue) · label boxes are not the cause

Hypothesis: CRG draws its defect away from the label box (which is the real defect's size, centred in the 64 window). Test (code/experiments/check_boxes.py, CPU): the changed pixels between each generated image and its background give the region the method actually drew; it is compared with the label box. As a reference, the same measurement on real PKU defects (photo vs clean board template).

Source (300 images)Images changedCentre offsetChanged area ÷ boxIoU (median)
real PKU defects (624)——0.150.15

dpmpaste100%0.5 px4.320.23

  • PKU's own boxes are loose: a defect fills about 15% of its box (5% for shorts). CRG's defects sit 2 px from the box centre and fill 14% of it, the same as real labels. Hypothesis rejected.
  • Copy-paste's high IoU comes from its pasted border; DPM-paste replaces the whole window. RePaint and the CoPaint approximation change nothing visible in 20% of images and elsewhere change an area 8 px off and twice the box size.

2026-11-17 (Tue) · CRG diagnostic 1: are the generated defects too weak or wrong?

diagnose_crg.py inspect (CPU): strongest local difference to the clean background inside the label box ("contrast", 0–255) and the number of changed pixels, for real defects and for each method.

ClassReal: contrast · changed pxCRGECICS
missing hole158 · 170153 · 125153 · 186
mouse bite50 · 10854 · 9355 · 102
open circuit48 · 7251 · 7453 · 80
short48 · 6257 · 7057 · 83
spur46 · 10950 · 8751 · 94
spurious copper46 · 13948 · 11749 · 122
  • Strength is not the problem: CRG's defects are as strong as real ones in every class, and slightly stronger for shorts.
  • Spurs: real PKU spurs are small, flat-topped bumps on the edge of a trace. CRG's spurs are often larger, rounded or trapezoid bulges, sometimes a widening of a whole pad or trace, and a few are hard to see. Several look like a normal board feature that happens to be wider.
  • Shorts: real shorts are a thin, straight copper bridge between two parallel traces. CRG's shorts are mostly bridges as well, but some are a grey blob or a widened trace instead of a bridge (columns 3, 5, 9 in the figure).
  • Working explanation: part of the synthetic spurs and shorts look like ordinary board structure, so the detector learns to fire on structure it should ignore, which is the precision loss above. This is a visual reading on 10 + 10 examples; diagnostic 2 tests it on the detector.

2026-11-17 (Tue) · GPU out of memory overnight

What happened. Mon 22:07 the 64-model run finished and the same process started the 256-model run, which needs about 12.3 GB instead of about 5 GB. At 22:08 it asked for 256 MB more and failed. Memory at that moment: training 8.1 GB (still growing), idle notebook kernel train_walkthrough 6.6 GB, idle kernel sample_checkpoints 1.2 GB, CoPaint generation 4.2 GB, a detector run 1.5 GB, desktop about 1.5 GB: 23.3 of 23.5 GB.

Why the pipeline then stood still. Its guard ("pause while the 256 training starts") looked only at the training log; after the crash the log never showed a training step again, so the guard waited all night. About 13 hours lost on training and experiments; no checkpoint or result was lost.

Fixes. The guard now checks that the training process is alive; generation waits for 8 GB free instead of 6 GB. The 256 training was restarted from step 50k at 11:05. The two idle kernels (Fri 13 Nov, sample_checkpoints.ipynb and Friday's train_walkthrough.ipynb) were stopped at about 11:50, freeing 7.9 GB; their results were already on disk. Free GPU memory with the 256 training running: about 9.7 GB.

2026-11-17 (Tue) · where the paper says CRG is better

From the CRG paper (TCSVT 2026), Sec. V, for comparison with our results:

  • Downstream detection (Table I): mAP@50–95 0.496 → 0.557 and recall 0.869 → 0.935; 2.5 points above DefFiller and 3.1 above ControlNet.
  • Hard structural classes (Fig. 4): spurious copper +21.1%, short +19.4%, spur +14.1% (the text says 17.1%), mouse bite +12.4%, open circuit +8.9%, missing hole +3.2%. On spur, RePaint and CoPaint lower the score.
  • Scaling (Fig. 5): 0.557 / 0.573 / 0.579 at 1× / 2× / 3×; RePaint peaks at 2× and then drops, CoPaint falls to 0.475 at 2×.
  • Inputs: only a defect-free image and a class label; no mask or text prompt.
  • Not in image metrics: KID×10³ 68.3, second worst (RePaint 8.8); the authors argue KID and LPIPS miss functional correctness.
  • In our setup so far, the classes where the paper reports the largest CRG gains (short, spur) are where CRG lowers precision. Possible reasons not controlled in the paper: its test images probably come from boards also used for training; and its gains are relative to its own baseline.

How the modules connect

Arrows point from a file to the files it imports. Green boxes run when you start sample_generation.py; the filled one holds the CRG algorithm itself.

runs during generation training only imported but not used by CRG

What happens when you generate one defect

Per defect line

sample_generation.py · process_images()
  1. Read the defect-free image and its .txt; convert each class cx cy to pixels.
  2. Place a 64×64 window centred on the point, clamped inside the image.
  3. Noise the whole image to step 30 of 250 (about t≈120 of 1000). The board stays recognisable.
  4. Cut the same window out of the noised image as the defect model's starting point.
  5. Run A_DDIMSampler.p_sample_loop over 110 scheduled steps, including two rounds of jumping back and re-noising.
  6. Save the full image to samples/, the patch to crop/, a comparison to grid/ and mask plots to temp/.

Per timestep

ddim.py · A_DDIMSampler.p_sample()
  1. 256 model predicts the clean image x̂₀ from x_t.
  2. 64 model predicts the clean patch ĉ₀ for the requested class.
  3. Build the defect mask from where ĉ₀ differs from the clean board, smoothed over time.
  4. Take 2 gradient steps on x_t to lower the loss below, with a line search that shrinks the step if the loss rises.
  5. Take a deterministic DDIM step (σ=0) for both the image and the patch.
1e5 · A_def ⊙ (crop(x̂₀) − ĉ₀)²            follow the defect model
1e4 · A_bg  ⊙ (crop(x̂₀) − crop(x_free))²   clean board inside window
5e4 · (1−window) ⊙ (x̂₀ − x_free)²          clean board outside window
1e-4 · ‖x_t − x_t,original‖²               stay close to start

Line counts are from the cloned commit. Use the filters to see only what generation needs, what training needs, or the leftovers you can ignore.

./ (top level)
sample_generation.py552 linesGenerationThe only runnable script. Loads the YAML config, finds defect-free images that have a .txt, builds both UNets and the sampler, then loops over every defect line. It skips combinations already in the output folder, so a stopped run can resume.

ddim.py1,116 linesGenerationThe core of the method. compute_attention_masks finds the defect area from the pixel difference; get_g_scha sets gradient steps per timestep; DDIMSampler is plain DDIM; A_DDIMSampler adds the two-model guidance, line search and time travel.
respace.py169 linesGenerationSpacedDiffusion keeps 250 of the 1000 training steps and maps timestep indices back for the UNet.

nn.py186 linesGenerationSmall building blocks: conv_nd, GroupNorm32, sinusoidal timestep_embedding, zero_module, update_ema, gradient checkpointing.
fp16_util.py281 linesGenerationConverts UNet layers to half precision; also has OpenAI's MixedPrecisionTrainer.
script_util.py405 linesGenerationDefault arguments and factories: create_model, and create_gaussian_diffusion, which builds whichever sampler class is passed as base_cls. Classifier factories are unused.
new_scheduler.py117 linesGenerationBuilds the timestep list. ddim_repaint_timesteps adds the jump-back segments; with the repo config it yields 110 steps starting at 29.
losses.py272 linesGenerationKL and discretised log-likelihood terms for training, plus mask_mse_loss / original_loss used by the sampler's simpler loss branch. A Laplacian pyramid loss is defined twice and never used.
scheduler.py310 linesUnusedRePaint jump schedules (get_schedule_jump). Imported by gaussian_diffusion.py but the CRG sampler uses new_scheduler.py instead.

Things to know before using it

  • sample_generation.py:315batch_size = 1 is hard-coded, and n_samples / n_iter from the README are never read. You get one image per label line; change seed for more.
  • confs/pcb_gen.ymlnum_iteration_optimize_xt: 4, gd_mask_radius and max_iter are ignored. Gradient steps per timestep come from g_scha (2).
  • ddim.py:848if t[0] / 10 == 0 is only true at t=0. It was probably meant as % 10.
  • ddim.py:5Unused from tkinter import Image fails on Python builds without Tk. Delete it if the import errors.
  • conf_mgt/conf_base.py:58__init__ is pass, so conf['missing'] raises KeyError while conf.missing returns None.
  • trainingNo train.py. You need about 40 lines that build the model with script_util, call load_data and run TrainLoop.
Run generation from the repo folder: python sample_generation.py --conf_path confs/pcb_gen.yml, after downloading both checkpoints into checkpoint/. Generation has been run once on the bundled sample; training has not been run yet. Longer notes: Graduate_Design/docs/CRG-DefectDiffuser_report.md.
